title: Judgments and claims, department by department
question: Which departments’ budgets carry the judgments and claims the City pays?
finding: The City’s ledger charges $557.7 million to its judgments and claims account from fiscal 2019 to 2026. The most sits with General City - Unallocated ($217.0 million); Public Utilities Commission ($110.4 million); City Attorney ($106.0 million); Municipal Transportation Agency ($98.4 million); Public Health ($12.5 million). By type the account holds judgements - legal fees ($315.9 million); litigation expenses ($86.8 million); litigation expenses-legal fees ($79.5 million); judgements - claims ($69.3 million).
how: The Controller’s Spending and Revenue table, spending lines whose account is “Judgments & Claims”, added up by department for fiscal 2019 to 2026; departments with under $250,000 in the period are left out. The peak column is the department’s largest single year.
limits: The account is where the payment was charged, which is usually the department whose work gave rise to the claim but can be a central fund. It includes litigation costs and legal fees as well as payments to claimants, and it does not match the financial report’s claim payments, which are measured differently. A large figure reflects the kind of work a department does (driving buses, policing, running hospitals, maintaining sewers) as much as how well it does it. The table does not say which of these payments the Board voted on.

sources.t: San Francisco Controller: Spending and Revenue, by department, account and fiscal year (DataSF)
